entities.name: PMID:25429227
observations: Prospective emergency-department study of 300 adults comparing fingerstick capillary and venous glucose by Masimo Radical-7 perfusion index.
In patients with abnormal vital signs, capillary–venous glucose consistency was better at PI ≥6; the abstract does not establish a universal direction or size of bias.

entities.name: PMID:18380985
observations: Prospective study of 85 critically ill patients; 15% of capillary strip values disagreed with laboratory glucose by >20%.
Low perfusion index independently predicted conflicting capillary glucose values, whereas whole-blood discrepancies were associated with hypotension and mottling.

entities.name: PMID:24801361
observations: In 181 paired samples from critically ill children, Bland–Altman bias was 7.4±17.7 mg/dL with acceptable PI versus 30.2±23.4 mg/dL with low PI ≤0.3.
Capillary glucose strip accuracy was lower than arterial or venous whole-blood testing in children with peripheral hypoperfusion.

entities.name: PMID:7894555
observations: Prospective study of 38 patients with shock found fingerstick glucose differed significantly from laboratory venous glucose, while venous bedside-meter results did not differ significantly from venous laboratory glucose.
Authors advised against fingerstick glucose analysis when tissue perfusion is inadequate.

entities.name: PMID:21478799
observations: In 337 paired measurements from 52 children with shock, mean capillary-versus-laboratory glucose difference was 6 mg/dL, although spread was wider at higher glucose values.
This study did not find a clinically important average discrepancy across shock groups, illustrating heterogeneity among populations and devices.
